sources.title: General School Requirements Related to Standards and Instruction, Section 100.2
sources.edition: Current official instructional-requirements summary reviewed October 18, 2026
sources.notes: Includes citizenship and DASA-related instruction, highway/traffic and fire/life safety, humane animal treatment in public elementary schools, conservation in public schools and other instructional overlays. Applicability differs by provision and school type. This summary is not the full official regulatory text.

sources.title: About the P-12 Learning Standards
sources.edition: Current official page reviewed October 18, 2026
sources.notes: State learning standards describe expected knowledge and skills; schools develop and adopt their own aligned curricula, instructional materials and sequences.

sources.title: Learning Standards for Health, Physical Education, and Family and Consumer Sciences
sources.edition: 1996 health and family and consumer sciences standards
sources.notes: Canonical document linked by the current Health Education page. This catalog uses its health and FACS coverage. Its physical education section has been superseded by the separate 2020 PE standards.

sources.title: Health Guidance and Resources
sources.edition: Current page; health curriculum guidance identified as updated April 25, 2014
sources.notes: The linked skills-based health curriculum guidance is not a mandate. Later required instruction and local review must supplement the older standards and guidance.

sources.title: New York State Prekindergarten Learning Standards: A Resource for School Success
sources.edition: Revised 2021
sources.notes: The current PE page directs prekindergarten physical development and health to this integrated early-learning resource, rather than assigning K-12 PE outcomes to PK.

sources.title: May 2018 Regents Joint Committee Report on Health Education
sources.edition: May 2018 adoption; effective July 1, 2018
sources.notes: Reports permanent adoption of health education regulatory amendments relating to mental health. It is an implementation overlay, not a new comprehensive 2026 health standards set.

sources.title: Erin's Law
sources.edition: 2019 law; current grade-band implementation resources
sources.notes: Public-school abuse and exploitation prevention instruction covers K-8. Suggested resource bands are K-2, 3-4, 5-6 and 7-8; curriculum remains a local decision.

sources.title: Heart Health Month: Supporting Cardiovascular Health Through Instruction
sources.edition: February 2026 memorandum
sources.notes: Explains senior-high hands-only CPR and AED instruction and cardiac-health awareness. Chat-based conceptual help cannot replace required practical instruction or emergency response.

sources.title: New York State Physical Education Learning Standards
sources.notes: Current PE standards linked from the official PE page. K-8 outcomes are grade-specific; high school uses Level 1 and Level 2. Only academic knowledge support is represented here.

sources.title: New York State Physical Education Learning Standards at a Glance
sources.edition: 2020 grade-level outcomes map
sources.notes: Shows the K-8 and HS Level 1/2 progression and directs PK to the separate early-learning standards. Strategies and tactics outcomes begin in grade 3, not in K-2.

sources.title: Physical Education Guidance and Resources
sources.edition: 2020 standards implementation roadmap; full implementation fall 2023 onward
sources.notes: Confirms the 2020 standards are in full implementation for 2026-2027; the combined 1996 document is not the current PE baseline.

sources.title: Personal Finance Education FAQ
sources.edition: March 2026 permanent adoption; effective March 25, 2026
sources.notes: Middle and high school band implementation begins 2026-2027; K-4 begins 2027-2028. Instruction is due by band end, not every grade. This is not a standalone credit or diploma requirement, and NYSED is not creating new personal finance standards.

sources.title: Personal Finance Topics and Grade-Band Learning Objectives
sources.edition: March 2026 learning objectives; K-4, 5-8 and 9-12
sources.notes: Five equally important topic areas support the instructional requirement. The published order does not prescribe local sequence. Objectives are distinct from an adopted standards set and use hypothetical financial situations to protect student privacy.

sources.title: NYSED Personal Finance Education Learning Objectives
sources.edition: March 2026
sources.notes: Official grade-band objectives resource. This catalog records scope only and does not transcribe every objective or relabel them as state learning standards.

sources.title: Career Development and Occupational Studies
sources.edition: Current NYSED CDOS standards listing and elementary/intermediate/commencement resources
sources.notes: Links the CDOS standards and their companion resource guide. Career development, integrated learning and universal foundation skills apply broadly; career-major technical content is specialized.

sources.title: Career Development and Occupational Studies Resource Guide with Core Curriculum
sources.edition: Current linked CDOS companion resource guide
sources.notes: Provides elementary, intermediate and commencement core content and sample activities. Sample classroom activities are adaptable examples, not a compulsory statewide lesson sequence.

sources.title: New York State Middle Level CTE Requirement
sources.edition: Current middle-level theme and content modules
sources.notes: Six cross-content themes and content modules guide local instruction. The page lists seven current content groups, including computer science; some introductory prose still says six.

sources.title: New York State Middle Level CTE Requirement FAQ
sources.edition: Current FAQ including 2022 addition of computer science
sources.notes: The 1.75-unit requirement applies in grades 5-8, with instruction able to begin in grade 5 under appropriate certification. Schools choose content areas; there is no required minimum number of different areas. General health education is distinct from CTE health sciences.

sources.title: Family and Consumer Sciences Learning Standards
sources.edition: Current NYSED state and national standards guidance
sources.notes: Identifies state FACS standards, national standards and the middle-level module framework. Commencement courses are locally selected and may serve mixed grades and abilities.

sources.title: Family and Consumer Sciences Course Offerings
sources.edition: Current intermediate grades 5-8 and commencement grades 9-12 guidance
sources.notes: The listed core and elective resources are expressly nonregulatory guidance. Schools determine offerings and sequence; practical facilities and qualified supervision remain necessary.

sources.title: New York State Career and Financial Management Curricular Framework
sources.edition: Updated November 2022
sources.notes: Career and financial management framework for CTE. Its role in approved CTE programs is separate from the new K-12 personal finance instructional requirement.

sources.title: Career and Financial Management Curricular Framework: Background
sources.edition: July 23, 2018 page with November 2022 framework update
sources.notes: One-half unit of CFM is required within NYSED-approved CTE programs and can be standalone or embedded; it is not a universal standalone high-school course. Grade 8 acceleration is possible.

sources.title: Career and Technical Education Program Content
sources.edition: Current secondary NYSED-approved CTE program guidance
sources.notes: Programs align with CDOS, appropriate state standards and industry standards, with appropriately certified faculty and practical components. A theory catalog does not create an approved CTE program or credential.

sources.title: Business and Marketing Learning Standards
sources.edition: Current CDOS and national standards guidance
sources.notes: Connects business and marketing to CDOS, including specialized business/information-systems content. Referenced national standards are not automatically new NYS academic standards or unrestricted source material.

sources.title: Business and Marketing FAQ
sources.edition: Current official FAQ reviewed October 18, 2026
sources.notes: Business curriculum and course choices are local. Topics include accounting/finance, management, marketing, entrepreneurship and professional communication. Academic-credit substitutions require local approval and applicable regulatory criteria.

sources.title: Agriculture Learning Standards
sources.edition: Current NYSED agriculture and AFNR guidance
sources.notes: NYSED states New York has no agriculture-specific academic standards. AFNR and career-cluster resources guide locally adapted programs, alongside classroom, supervised experience and leadership components.

sources.title: Health Sciences Learning Standards
sources.edition: Current NYSED CDOS and health-science core guidance
sources.notes: NCHSE Health Science Standards are acceptable for developing the health-sciences core. This occupational field is distinct from general health education and includes supervised practical requirements.

sources.title: Student Career Areas in Trade and Technical Education
sources.edition: Current NYSED career-area overview
sources.notes: Describes construction, transportation, manufacturing, visual/communication arts, human/public services and information technology. Listed occupations are examples, not required courses or permission for unsupervised practical instruction.

sources.title: New York State Learning Standards for the Arts Implementation Guide
sources.edition: 2017 arts standards implementation guide, current linked edition
sources.notes: Five disciplines use creating, presenting/performing/producing, responding and connecting. PK-8 indicators are grade-specific; high school uses Proficient, Accomplished and Advanced levels rather than fixed grades 9, 10, 11 and 12.

sources.title: New York State Visual Arts Learning Standards at a Glance
sources.notes: Canonical visual arts standards linked by the current Arts page. This subject covers art literacy, interpretation, design thinking and historical/cultural connections; it is not a complete studio curriculum.

sources.title: New York State Music Learning Standards at a Glance
sources.notes: General music covers PK-8. Other strands include composition/theory, harmonizing instruments, technology and traditional/emerging ensembles. This catalog retains theory, listening and historical knowledge rather than ensemble or instrumental performance instruction.

sources.title: New York State Media Arts Learning Standards at a Glance
sources.notes: Canonical media arts standards linked by the current Arts page. Conceptual tutoring can support interpretation, planning, ethics and critique without producing the student's assessed media work.

sources.title: New York State Theater Learning Standards at a Glance
sources.notes: Canonical theater standards linked by the current Arts page. The catalog represents dramatic literacy and contextual/design analysis, not acting proficiency or a replacement for rehearsal.

sources.title: New York State Dance Learning Standards at a Glance
sources.notes: Canonical dance standards linked by the current Arts page. The catalog covers vocabulary, composition concepts, interpretation and context; physical technique and performance require qualified supervision.

sources.title: NYSED Guidance for HIV/AIDS Prevention Education
sources.edition: May 2025 cover; revised April 2025 body
sources.notes: Age-appropriate AIDS instruction is part of K–6 sequential health and required 7–8 and 9–12 health courses. Broader comprehensive sexuality education remains locally selected; school procedures govern the limited prevention-method exemption.

subjects.name: Health Education

frameworks.notes: PK health and physical development use the integrated early-learning resource.
Elementary, intermediate and commencement expectations; schools choose the grade sequence and approved content.
Mental health is part of health education; implementation is not limited to the older 1996 wording.
Use age-appropriate, school-approved abuse-prevention material and the actual local sequence.

frameworks.version: HIV/AIDS prevention guidance, revised April 2025, May 2025 cover
frameworks.notes: An age-appropriate required-topic overlay within health; school selects curriculum and manages any applicable prevention-method parent exemption. Not a separate annual course.

topics: Personal care, food and activity habits
Naming feelings and asking for help
Changing bodies and age-appropriate family-life concepts
Mental health literacy and coping skills
Healthy relationships, boundaries and online safety
Evaluating health influences and setting goals
Mental wellness, communication and help seeking
Age-appropriate HIV/AIDS knowledge, prevention and stigma reduction within school-approved health instruction

tutoring_scope: Explain approved health concepts and vocabulary
Practice communication, decision-making and goal-setting scenarios
Help evaluate the reliability of health information
limitations: Focus groups are planning summaries, not a mandated grade-by-grade syllabus.
Use the school's approved, developmentally appropriate health curriculum, including later required instruction.
Tutoring does not diagnose or provide individualized medical or mental health treatment.
Knowledge support does not replace practical CPR instruction, professional care or school safeguarding procedures.

School-approved age-appropriate HIV/AIDS materials and applicable prevention-method parent exemptions remain school decisions; this catalog does not implement consent/exemption management or imply a universal comprehensive-sexuality syllabus.

subjects.name: Physical Education Knowledge

frameworks.notes: PK physical development and health are separate from the K-12 PE outcomes.
K-8 indicators are grade-specific. HS Level 1 and Level 2 require local placement and must not be equated automatically to particular grades.

topics: Safe movement and healthy activity habits
Movement concepts and simple game strategies
Social responsibility and community activity resources

tutoring_scope: Explain rules, concepts, fitness vocabulary and planning
Discuss activity choices, social responsibility and wellness
Support written PE assignments and conceptual reflection
limitations: This is academic support for PE, not a substitute for physical participation or required PE credit.
No claim of motor-skill, sport, exercise-technique or fitness-performance assessment.
The 1996 combined health/PE/FACS document is not the current PE standard set.
Follow the school's actual grade or high-school proficiency placement and qualified supervision.

subjects.name: Family and Consumer Sciences

frameworks.notes: Elementary, intermediate and commencement expectations can be integrated locally; they do not prescribe a separate FACS course in every grade.
FACS is one possible lens for middle-level CTE; schools determine their module mix.

tutoring_scope: Explain FACS concepts and applied reading or mathematics
Support consumer decisions using hypothetical scenarios
Prepare for school-selected course knowledge and reflective tasks
limitations: School syllabus and course offerings determine scope and order; national guidance is not automatically a NYS mandate.
Cooking, food handling, sewing, equipment use and care activities require suitable facilities and qualified supervision.
Conceptual tutoring does not certify practical skill or award course credit.

subjects.name: Personal Finance

frameworks.notes: These are instructional learning objectives, not a newly adopted NYS standards set. Schools choose sequence within each band.
Grades 5-8 and 9-12 begin implementation in 2026-2027; K-4 begins in 2027-2028, with earlier local instruction permitted.

topics: Money, needs, wants and everyday choices
Saving goals and introductory investing concepts
Gross pay, net pay and taxes
Budgeting, housing costs and consumer decisions
Loans, credit reports and education financing
Pay, benefits, labor markets and hypothetical tax forms
Banking, retirement accounts and investment risk

tutoring_scope: Explain the five personal-finance topic areas
Guide calculations and reasoning with fictitious financial examples
Support locally embedded instruction or an approved local course
limitations: The 2026 requirement is end-of-band instruction, not instruction in every grade or a standalone graduation credit.
K-4 coverage is available for planning or early local adoption in 2026-2027; its required phase begins in 2027-2028.
Incoming grade 5 and grade 9 cohorts in 2026-2027 must receive instruction by band end; initial-year exiting students may not have completed it.
Use fictional income, tax and account data; do not request family financial records or individualized investment advice.
The catalog does not determine credit, diploma eligibility or financial-product recommendations.

subjects.name: Career Development and Occupational Studies

frameworks.version: Current CDOS elementary, intermediate and commencement standards
frameworks.notes: Career development, integrated learning and universal foundation skills support all learners; specialized career-major expectations require an actual program.
CFM may support approved CTE programs and locally selected courses; grade 8 is an acceleration option, not a universal placement.

topics: How school skills connect to everyday work

tutoring_scope: Explain career vocabulary and pathway research methods
Help students reflect on strengths and plan their own next steps
Support workplace scenarios and applied academic reasoning
limitations: Follow the school's actual career plan, syllabus and program expectations.
Tutoring does not establish a CDOS credential, technical endorsement, work-readiness certification or supervised work hours.
Students author their own career materials and reflections; occupational practice and placements require school supervision.

subjects.name: Visual Arts and Art History

frameworks.notes: PK-8 indicators are individual-grade expectations; HS Proficient, Accomplished and Advanced levels are not fixed school years. Topic groups below are catalog summaries.

topics: Elements, design choices and visual vocabulary
Design inquiry, curation and artistic intent

tutoring_scope: Explain visual-art vocabulary and art-historical context
Guide observation, interpretation and critique
Discuss planning choices without making the student's assessed work
limitations: Use the school's syllabus, selected works and actual HS proficiency level.
This knowledge scope does not replace studio practice, portfolio assessment, art-credit requirements or supervised material use.
External images and media require source review and appropriate rights before student presentation.

subjects.name: Music Literacy, Theory and History

frameworks.notes: General music is PK-8; HS classroom music includes composition/theory and technology. Other strands have their own levels; the catalog excludes ensemble and instrumental performance as core tutoring.

topics: Music in daily life and culture

tutoring_scope: Explain notation, theory, form and musical vocabulary
Support listening analysis and historical research
Guide students' own musical reasoning and critique
limitations: Use the school's approved syllabus, chosen strand and actual proficiency level.
Band, choir, instrumental technique, rehearsal and performance certification are outside core tutoring scope.
Tutoring does not compose assessed student work or establish performance proficiency or course credit.
Audio and video examples require reviewed sources and appropriate rights.

subjects.name: Media Arts Studies

frameworks.notes: PK-8 grade indicators and HS Proficient/Accomplished/Advanced levels; grouped topics here are coverage summaries, not a replacement sequence.

topics: Cultural context, ethics and critical analysis

tutoring_scope: Explain media-art concepts and production vocabulary
Guide analysis, planning and reflective critique
Help compare source, audience and artistic choices
limitations: Use the school's syllabus, tools and actual proficiency placement.
Students produce their own assessed media; tutoring does not certify production skills or replace supervised practical work.
External media must pass the application's school review and rights checks before use.

subjects.name: Theatre Studies

frameworks.notes: PK-8 grade indicators and three HS proficiency levels; placement follows the school's course, not an assumed age-to-level mapping.

tutoring_scope: Explain dramatic vocabulary, structure and context
Guide script reading and evidence-based interpretation
Discuss design and criticism without writing assessed work
limitations: Use the school's approved texts, syllabus and proficiency placement.
Acting, rehearsal, stagecraft practice and equipment use require qualified supervision.
Conceptual tutoring does not establish performance proficiency or replace practical course assessment.

subjects.name: Dance Studies

frameworks.notes: PK-8 individual-grade indicators and HS Proficient, Accomplished and Advanced levels; this subject covers knowledge rather than physical technique.

topics: Shape, space, time and movement words

tutoring_scope: Explain dance vocabulary, history and composition concepts
Guide observation, interpretation and critique
Support written or conceptual course work
limitations: Use the school's approved syllabus, reviewed examples and actual proficiency level.
Physical dance technique, conditioning, partner work and performance assessment require qualified supervision.
This subject does not claim to replace participation or demonstrate practical dance proficiency.

subjects.name: Middle-Level Career and Technical Studies

frameworks.version: Current theme and content module framework
frameworks.notes: Local programs combine common themes with selected CTE content areas; every content area need not be a separate required course.
Grades 5-8 collectively carry the 1.75-unit middle-level requirement, with appropriate certified teaching.

topics: Sustainability through locally selected CTE fields

tutoring_scope: Explain concepts from the school's selected CTE modules
Connect academic skills to career scenarios
Help reason about project plans and reflect on learning
limitations: Use the school's actual module selection, syllabus and grade sequence.
Seven possible content areas include agriculture, business/marketing, computing, FACS, health sciences, technology and trade/technical; all seven are not compulsory separate courses.
Theory help does not replace certified CTE instruction, safe laboratories, supervised practical work or the required units of study.
Computing, engineering and technology have separate catalog subjects; this entry records the shared middle-level framework.

subjects.name: Business and Marketing Studies

frameworks.version: Current NYSED CDOS and national guidance
frameworks.notes: School-selected business courses align to applicable CDOS and program standards; this is not a mandatory statewide course sequence.

tutoring_scope: Explain business and marketing vocabulary
Guide case analysis and applied calculations
Support the student's own planning and professional communication
limitations: Local elective: follow the school's approved syllabus, prerequisites and available course offerings.
School approval and regulatory criteria govern credit substitutions and approved CTE program status.
Tutoring does not replace supervised business projects, workplace experiences or assessed student authorship.

subjects.name: Accounting and Business Finance

frameworks.notes: An elective specialization under business/finance; detailed coverage and external standards depend on the local course.

topics: Ethics and accuracy in financial information

tutoring_scope: Explain locally assigned accounting methods
Guide worked reasoning using fictional records
Help students find and understand calculation or classification errors
limitations: Local elective: use the school's syllabus, accounting conventions and prerequisites.
Accounting is not automatically a required mathematics course or approved credit substitution.
Use fictional records; tutoring does not provide professional financial advice, certify bookkeeping or replace supervised coursework.

subjects.name: Entrepreneurship

frameworks.notes: Entrepreneurship is a possible business or FACS-linked offering, with locally determined depth and sequence.

tutoring_scope: Explain enterprise concepts and model hypothetical choices
Guide students' own market reasoning and plan revisions
Support calculations and critique without writing the project
limitations: Local elective: use the school's approved syllabus, project rules and prerequisites.
This scope is not a statewide required course or authority to start financial accounts, transact or contact external parties.
Practical enterprise projects require teacher supervision; students author their own assessed work.

subjects.name: Agriculture, Food and Natural Resource Studies

frameworks.notes: NYSED identifies no agriculture-specific NYS academic standards; local programs may use national AFNR guidance alongside applicable state standards.

tutoring_scope: Explain concepts from the school's agriculture program
Connect agricultural questions to science and quantitative reasoning
Support analysis of food systems, resources and careers
limitations: Local elective: use the school's syllabus, selected AFNR pathway and prerequisites.
National AFNR guidance must not be labelled as a separate adopted NYS agriculture academic standards set.
Animal care, fieldwork, food production, biotechnology laboratories and equipment require qualified supervision.
Theory support does not establish practical competence, occupational certification or supervised work hours.

subjects.name: Health Sciences Career Studies

frameworks.version: Current CDOS and acceptable NCHSE core guidance
frameworks.notes: A local health-sciences program selects and aligns its academic and technical core; this is not general health education.

topics: Academic foundations for locally selected health-science theory

tutoring_scope: Explain approved career and health-science concepts
Support reading, vocabulary and hypothetical case reasoning
Help prepare for knowledge components of a school-selected course
limitations: Local elective: follow the school's approved syllabus, prerequisites and program standards.
Health-sciences CTE is distinct from the required general health education course.
Tutoring does not provide clinical advice or certify patient-care, laboratory or emergency-treatment competence.
Clinical placements and hands-on skills require appropriate qualified supervision and cannot be replaced by chat.

subjects.name: Child Development and Human Development

frameworks.notes: Possible local offerings include lifespan studies, child/adolescent development, parenting, early childhood, gerontology and human-service careers.

tutoring_scope: Explain approved developmental and family-study concepts
Guide comparison of ideas using the course's sources
Support hypothetical observations and student-authored reflection
limitations: Local elective: use the school's syllabus and selected course focus; these are not mandatory separate courses in every high-school year.
This scope does not diagnose development, provide individualized psychological care or replace qualified child-care instruction.
Observations, placements and direct caregiving require school-approved supervision and privacy protection.

subjects.name: Nutrition and Food Science

frameworks.version: Current FACS food and nutrition course guidance
frameworks.notes: Food science, food preparation/nutrition, wellness and food-related pathways are locally selected course options, not a fixed statewide sequence.

topics: Food systems, culture and related careers

tutoring_scope: Explain school-approved nutrition and food-science concepts
Guide label reading and hypothetical planning calculations
Support analysis of food systems and laboratory concepts
limitations: Local elective: follow the school's syllabus, prerequisites and laboratory procedures.
Food preparation, preservation, allergen management and equipment use require qualified supervision.
Tutoring does not prescribe diets, manage medical conditions or certify food-handling competence.

subjects.name: Housing, Textiles and Consumer Design

frameworks.version: Current FACS clothing/textiles and housing/environment guidance
frameworks.notes: Schools may select clothing, fashion, interiors, home furnishings or related design courses and define their own sequence.

topics: Living spaces, needs and resource choices

tutoring_scope: Explain consumer, material and design concepts
Support measurement, planning and reasoned critique
Connect design choices to needs, costs and environmental context
limitations: Local elective: use the school's syllabus, selected design field and prerequisites.
Sewing, cutting, construction, tool use and practical installations require qualified supervision.
Tutoring does not produce assessed designs, establish trade competence or substitute for a practical portfolio.

subjects.name: Trade and Technical Career Studies

frameworks.version: Current NYSED trade and technical career overview
frameworks.notes: Local programs select a career area and its applicable state and industry standards; the overview is not a universal trade curriculum.
Approved programs require more than conceptual content, including qualified faculty and applicable practical requirements.

topics: Reading technical information in a selected trade

tutoring_scope: Explain concepts from a school-approved trade syllabus
Support technical reading, units, measurement and hypothetical calculations
Help reason about safety and work planning without directing physical operations
limitations: Local elective: require the school's specific trade syllabus, prerequisites and approved technical references.
This broad entry does not imply every occupation or certification standard has been ingested.
No unsupervised machinery operation, electrical work, construction, vehicle repair, cosmetology procedures, clinical work or other practical skill certification.
Qualified supervision, laboratories, workplace placements and industry assessment remain the school's responsibility.
Engineering, technology and computing are represented by separate catalog subjects rather than duplicated here.

transitions.title: Personal finance instruction permanently adopted
transitions.finding: The March 2026 amendment became permanently effective March 25, 2026. It creates a phased instructional requirement, not a new standalone diploma credit or new state learning standards set.

transitions.title: Middle and high school personal finance phase begins
transitions.finding: Implementation starts in the 5-8 and 9-12 bands in 2026-2027. Incoming grade 5 and grade 9 students must receive instruction by the end of those bands; students exiting a band during the initial year may not yet have received it. Schools choose delivery within each band.

transitions.title: Elementary personal finance phase follows
transitions.finding: Required K-4 implementation begins in 2027-2028. Catalog coverage in 2026-2027 supports planning or earlier local instruction and must not be presented as an already effective requirement in every elementary grade.

transitions.title: 2020 PE standards are the current full-implementation baseline
transitions.finding: NYSED identifies full implementation from fall 2023 onward. For 2026-2027, use the 2020 PE standards rather than the PE portion of the combined 1996 health/PE/FACS document.

transitions.title: Middle-level CTE includes computer science
transitions.finding: The official FAQ says computer science was added as a seventh CTE content area in 2022. Retain all seven current areas despite older prose referring to six; school-selected areas and appropriate certification still control local delivery.

review_notes.finding: School planning must include applicable highway/traffic safety, fire and arson prevention, injury/life safety and emergency-reporting education; citizenship, civility, anti-bullying/discrimination and safe Internet use; humane treatment of animals/birds in public elementary schools; and natural-resource conservation in public schools. These are cross-curricular instructional overlays, not newly invented standalone required courses. Drills, emergency practice and supervision remain outside chat-only tutoring.

This is a reviewed coverage and provenance catalog using original topic summaries. It is not a complete standards transcription, a state-issued curriculum, a human-approved teaching corpus or evidence that lessons are ready for student use.

Source review establishes official provenance and applicable scope. PDF links were verified through current NYSED pages and available official search excerpts; full indicator extraction and exact-byte review are not claimed, so no fabricated content hashes or official indicator IDs are supplied.

Every listed grade is eligible catalog coverage, not a mandate to teach a separate course in that year. PK-8 arts indicators and K-8 PE indicators retain their original grade structure; broader focus groupings summarize planning scope. HS arts proficiency levels and PE Level 1/2 require school placement, not an invented grade-to-level mapping.

Personal finance's March 2026 objectives guide a phased K-12 instructional requirement. They are distinct from adopted standards and from the half-unit CFM content required inside NYSED-approved CTE programs. Neither establishes a universal standalone personal-finance graduation credit.

Only explanation, theory, analysis and student-authored reasoning are represented. Band/instrument performance, sport and dance technique, studio proficiency, CPR practice, clinical work, machinery operation and supervised occupational skills cannot be completed or certified by this tutoring catalog.

National, industry and career-cluster references support local CTE design but are not automatically adopted NYS academic standards. Further source/rights review and school-specific syllabus alignment are required before ingestion or student-visible teaching.

The health baseline must be read with later required instruction and current local health policy. The source catalog covers selected important overlays and is not an exhaustive legal-compliance checklist or a new 2026 health standards adoption.

Current NYSED guidance identifies AIDS instruction within K–6 sequential health and required health courses at grades 7–8 and 9–12. Apply age-appropriate school-selected curriculum and school-managed prevention-method exemption procedures; broader comprehensive sexuality education is locally chosen.
